rivalry.rationale: India men's grooming (INR 186.3bn / ~US$1.94bn 2025, Euromonitor HIGH, +9%) is contested by FMCG incumbents in the largest baskets (haircare, deodorants) plus razors, while men's skincare and beard care — the fastest-growing, corridor-whitespace slices — draw new D2C entrants. Established incumbency plus an emerging challenger front makes intensity high.

buyer_power.rationale: E-commerce is 30-35% of urban men's-grooming sales (online ~27% share, fastest-growing), so beauty platforms and q-commerce are increasingly decisive gatekeepers, while the mass balance still moves through fragmented GT/MT. Channel leverage is rising but not yet dominant across the whole basket.

supplier_power.rationale: Men's-grooming D2C relies on the same fragmented third-party contract-manufacturing base (MOQs ~500 units) and domestic ingredient suppliers, so input-side bargaining power over brand owners is low.
evidence: india_findings.yaml supply_chain: third-party CMs (Gorgeous Cosmos, IndiaMART), MOQ ~500; Galaxy Surfactants / Fine Organics

new_entrant_threat.rationale: Men's skincare is explicitly the corridor's whitespace #4 (underserved vs toiletries) and is the fastest-growing slice, so an underserved, growing lane sits open to asset-light contract-manufactured D2C and to K-beauty import entrants — with CDSCO registration the main friction for the imported route.
evidence: corridor.yaml whitespace: 'Men's K-beauty (baseline whitespace #4 — men's skincare underserved vs toiletries)'

india_findings.yaml new_players: D2C funding; corridor.yaml regulation CDSCO (import friction)

substitutes.rationale: Men's-dedicated products compete with unisex/family grooming and the basket is shifting from toiletries toward skincare — men trading traditional shave/toiletry spend into dedicated skincare and beard care evidences substitution within the segment. Directional, given basket-definition variance.
evidence: mens_grooming.json IN IBEF note: haircare+deo largest but skincare/beard care fastest-growing (spend migrating within basket)
mens_grooming.json IN IMARC 'male toiletries' 46.8% basket includes shampoo/body wash/face wash (definitional overlap with unisex care)

overall.rationale: India men's grooming is well-evidenced, growing +9%, with low supplier power and an explicit, underserved men's-skincare whitespace (corridor #4) that suits a K-beauty entrant. But incumbents own the large toiletries/deo/hair baskets, rivalry is high, and rising channel concentration adds gatekeeper cost. Attractive on the skincare whitespace specifically rather than the broad basket.
evidence: mens_grooming.json IN size + growth (HIGH); corridor.yaml whitespace #4
